era.JPN: Japan: the age of the samurai
region.kyoto.intro: Kyoto is the ancient city of the emperors: the palace, hundreds of temples, silk workshops and noisy markets. Court nobles live here, monks, merchants and warriors flock here - and war and fire keep coming back here too.
region.kamakura.intro: Kamakura is a warriors' town between wooded hills and the sea. From 1185 the shoguns and their Hōjō regents rule from here, samurai from all over the country come to fight land suits, and the new Zen monasteries teach people to sit in silence.
region.hakata.intro: Hakata is Japan's gateway on Kyushu. Junks from China and Korea bring silk, porcelain and copper coins into the harbour, and a stone wall built against the Mongol fleets runs along the shore.
region.sakai.intro: Sakai is a rich, moated trading town on the bay. A council of merchants runs it, not a lord; here they brew sake, forge guns and drink tea from bowls worth more than an estate.
region.echigo.intro: Echigo is a snowy rice province on the Sea of Japan. In winter the drifts rise above the roofs, in summer young and old stand knee-deep in the paddies, and the local lords live by feuding with their neighbours.
